summary: Full backend + E2E frontend regression of PT SJM sawit app. Created pytest suite (27 tests, 25 pass = 92.6%) covering auth/signup-approval/reject, owners master, transaction CRUD + all validations, generator atomicity & schedule rules, analytics filters, Excel formula export, batch archiving. Ran 4 Playwright E2E flows on the public URL: signup->pending->approve->login->reject, owners add/edit, manual transaction add/edit/delete + validations, voucher preview/print, delete-by-date isolation, generator (infeasible detail toast + exact 6450 Kg), dashboard date filter, Excel download, New-bulan batch archive + batch switching. Two real backend defects found: duplicate transaction_code after a delete, and no brute-force lockout (playbook requirement). DB restored to clean seed state (admin + 4 seed owners, 0 transactions, BATCH-2026-09 active).

critical.issue: transaction_code is generated from count_documents(batch) + 1, so after deleting a transaction the next insert re-uses an existing code. Reproduced: create 2 tx (…-001, …-002), delete …-001, next create returns …-002 (duplicate). Codes are printed on the weighbridge voucher, so duplicates are a finance/audit defect. Use a monotonic counter per batch/month (findAndModify sequence) or max(existing seq)+1.
No brute-force protection: 6+ consecutive wrong passwords all return 401 with no lockout/throttle (playbook requires lockout after 5 fails, expected 423/429).

minor.issue: Admin email+password are hardcoded in server.py (ADMIN_PASSWORD='178910') and the seed only inserts when missing - it never re-syncs the password hash of an existing admin, so changing the constant has no effect (playbook item 5 not implemented). Move to env vars and update the hash on startup when it differs.

JWT_SECRET is not present in backend/.env, so secrets.token_hex(32) is regenerated on every backend restart -> every issued token becomes invalid and all users are silently logged out after a restart/deploy. Persist JWT_SECRET in .env.

CORS_ORIGINS='*' combined with allow_credentials=True is an invalid CORS combination for credentialed requests; and auth uses a localStorage Bearer token instead of the httpOnly cookie the auth playbook asks for (XSS token theft risk).
batch_id is taken from the query string without checking it is the ACTIVE batch, so transactions inside an archived batch can be mass-deleted (spec says the operation is limited to the active batch).
delete returns {success:true} even when nothing was deleted (protected admin) and approve returns {success:false} when the user was already approved - misleading response semantics for the UI toast.
No DELETE endpoint for owners - test/incorrect master rows can never be removed (only the active flag). Upsert also allows unlimited duplicate names.

Currently mocked, but when RESEND_API_KEY is set the synchronous resend SDK call is awaited inline in login / save_tx / delete_day, blocking the event loop on every request. Move to a background task/executor with a timeout.

ui_bugs.issue: Sonner toasts render top-right on top of the batch selector and the 'New bulan' button; generator error toasts last 9s and fully cover both controls, blocking interaction. Offset the toaster or move header actions.

Every batch created by 'New bulan' is labelled with the current month, so multiple batches show the identical text 'September 2026 · Arsip' and cannot be told apart (only the hidden id differs). Label with period/sequence or creation date.
load()/refresh()/loadUsers() have no catch and no loading/empty-error state; an API failure produces an unhandled promise rejection and a silently blank dashboard (no error UI, no retry).

integration_issues.issue: After a feasible run the success toast could not be found in the DOM ~4.5s after submit while the previous 9s error toast was still visible; the data itself was written correctly (5 rows, exact 6.450 Kg) and the modal closed. Likely toast stacking/timing - verify the success toast is not hidden behind the long-lived error toast.

issues: Native browser date inputs are used (render as US mm/dd/yyyy) in an Indonesian app instead of a localized/shadcn calendar - inconsistent with dd/mm/yyyy shown everywhere else
The two date inputs are unlabeled and separated by a very large empty gap, so it is unclear which is start and which is end
Same native picker issue on delete-day-date-input and tx-date-input
Edit pencil sits alone on a second row at the bottom-left of each card, visually detached from the card content
When a batch has no transactions the two charts render as empty axes boxes with no 'no data' message
Left brand panel has a very large vertical empty area between the headline and the 07:00-16:00 stamp on 1080p

action_items: Fix duplicate transaction_code generation after deletes (use a persistent per-batch sequence, not count_documents).
Add brute-force lockout/throttling on POST /api/auth/login (lock after 5 failures) per the auth playbook.
Persist JWT_SECRET in backend/.env so restarts do not invalidate all sessions; move admin email/password to env and re-sync the admin hash on startup.
Set explicit CORS origins (not '*') when allow_credentials=True; consider httpOnly cookie session as the playbook requires.
Restrict DELETE /api/transactions/date/{date} to the active batch.
Give each batch a unique human label so archived batches are distinguishable in batch-selector-dropdown.
Move the Toaster so it does not cover batch-selector-dropdown / new-batch-button.
Add error/loading states (and .catch) to load()/refresh() in App.js; replace native date inputs with the localized/shadcn date picker.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py:130 - transaction_code derived from count_documents is not collision-safe; also the whole save_tx body is a single 700+ char line, making it unreviewable/untestable.
server.py:23 - JWT_SECRET falls back to a random value; sessions break on every restart.
server.py:21-22 - credentials hardcoded in source instead of env vars.
server.py:133 - delete_day trusts the client-supplied batch_id, allowing mass deletion inside archived batches.
server.py:33-43 - notify() executes a blocking third-party SDK call inside async request handlers.
App.js - entire app in one file with extremely long single-line JSX components; no .catch/loading states around API calls.

rca_of_the_issue: Duplicate transaction_code: save_tx builds the sequence as count_documents({batch_id}) + 1. Deleting any transaction lowers the count, so the next insert regenerates an already-used sequence number (reproduced deterministically in test_tx_code.py). Fix by storing a per-batch counter document and using find_one_and_update($inc) or by computing max existing sequence + 1. Brute-force: login has no attempt counter/lockout collection, so credential stuffing is unthrottled.
